home patch.definition: The place you bird regularly and know better than anyone else does.

patch tick.definition: A bird new for your patch - not a lifer, but the one that makes a local birder's day.

twitch.definition: To travel for one specific rare bird that somebody else has already found.

self-found.definition: A rarity you found yourself instead of twitching. Worth more to most birders.

mega.definition: A seriously rare bird - the kind people drive through the night for.

stakeout.definition: A known bird sitting still enough at one spot that you can go and get it.

tick.definition: A species added to a list. A year tick counts for the year, not for life.
tick.usedIn: Leaderboard Ticks and My Year List

lifer.definition: A species seen by a birder for the first time ever in their life.
lifer.usedIn: My Year List and species cards

nemesis bird.definition: A species that repeatedly eludes a birder despite their attempts to see it.

dip.definition: To go for a bird and not see it. The risk every chase carries.

big day.definition: A day run to see as many species as possible, usually on a planned route.

fallout.definition: Weather forcing migrating birds down in numbers, all at once.

vagrant.definition: A bird found well outside its regular geographic range.

armchair tick.definition: A species you gain because taxonomists split one bird into two - without seeing anything new.

spark bird.definition: The species that triggered a lasting passion for birding.

peep.definition: Any of the small, maddeningly similar Calidris sandpipers.

LBJ.definition: Little brown job - a blanket term for small, drab brown birds that are difficult to distinguish.

crippler.definition: A spectacularly striking rarity - an enthusiastic, subjective reaction rather than a measurable category.
crippler.usedIn: Glossary only; never assigned by the app

gripped off.definition: To miss a bird that other birders managed to see, usually after making the same attempt.
gripped off.usedIn: Glossary only; never used to judge a chase

stringer.definition: A birder suspected of reporting birds they did not see or could not reliably identify.
stringer.usedIn: Glossary only; never applied to a person by the app

twitcher.definition: A dedicated birder who travels considerable distances to see target species and add them to a list.

Patagonia Picnic Table Effect.definition: One rarity attracts many birders to a place, and their added searching produces more unusual discoveries there.

pish.definition: To make repeated pishing sounds in an attempt to draw songbirds out of cover.

pelagic.definition: Living on the open ocean, or birding offshore for species associated with it.

siesta time.definition: The quiet middle of the afternoon, when many birds are less active and harder to find.

SOB.definition: Spouse of birder - humorous shorthand for a birder's non-birding partner.
SOB.usedIn: Glossary only; never used to label a person by the app

butterbutt.definition: An affectionate nickname for the Yellow-rumped Warbler, named for its bright yellow rump patch.

purple pooper.definition: A joking nickname for the Gray Catbird, inspired by the purple stains left after it eats dark berries.
purple pooper.usedIn: Glossary only; never used as the app's species name
